_doc: AI BASELINE -- the fixed, known cost figure. David's ruling, 14 Aug 2026: model selection cannot be automated when a silent change can move profit from good to very bad. This file pins the approved model AND ITS COST ENVELOPE per task tier. The envelope matters as much as the model id: the same model at 10 uncapped images costs several times the same model at a capped resolution, so a pure model-id register would let cost drift with the id unchanged.
failover_rule: Two different tests, deliberately. AUTO-FAILOVER (anthropic) must stay within the continuity tolerance of 6.0x base -- it is chosen for continuity, not price, but the cost of continuity must be bounded. LAST RESORT (scaleway) is COST-EXEMPT because it is reached when the alternative is being down or banned -- but reaching it must ALERT and be time-boxed. Note the consequence of putting the cheapest lane at the base: every failover is now a cost increase by definition. That is accepted; what is not acceptable is that it would currently be INVISIBLE in the spend log (D3).

equivalence_test.rule: The candidate model has an entry on ai_price_card.json. No price, no swap.
gate_by_tier passes for the exact tier -- the gate tuple is (model, tier, prompt version, effort, sampling), never a model-wide boolean.
Worst-case cost per CALL within the envelope is <= baseline worst case x tolerance. Note: per-Mtok price is NOT the test -- token shapes differ.
Passes the golden set on the LIVE seam, not on the dead failover/ package.
The change is written with actor, prior value, new value, reason and timestamp. Today POST /admin/flags writes NONE of these.

incumbency_review._doc: David's ruling forbids automating the SWITCH. It does not forbid automating the CHALLENGE -- and if the review is manual too, inertia becomes the decision, taken by default every day. So: automatic detection and surfacing, manual decision. scripts/ai_challenger_board.py never switches anything; it puts the numbers in front of David so silence stops being an answer.
incumbency_review.rule_incumbent: The sitting model is re-auditioned on the golden set every 90 days at the PINNED effort level it actually runs at in production. The price card's funnel step 4 says sitting models are not re-auditioned continuously -- correct, continuously is wasteful; never is worse, because a model that never takes the test can never fail it.
incumbency_review.rule_blocked: Any lane marked BLOCKED BY PROCESS must carry a named owner and a target date. A lane excluded for a process reason rather than a merit reason is a decision nobody made.
incumbency_review.escalation: A CHALLENGER that clears the 30% bar at equal-or-better capability is surfaced to R4. The board never acts.

capability_note.aa_index_caveat: AA index scores are NOT like-for-like. claude-haiku-4-5 carries effort_matched=false (benchmarked in reasoning mode, the app runs default), while mistral-medium-3.5-128b carries effort_matched=true. Haiku's 29.58 is therefore FLATTERED relative to how it actually runs, so mistral's nominal +1.25% edge is probably a real, if modest, one. Any procurement decision must re-score at the production effort level, not accept the leaderboard number.
capability_note.scaleway_role: The card's own words: 'CONTINUITY/JURISDICTION standby, not a cheap lane.' It is one model across all four tiers (ONE-MODEL STANDBY, David 18 Jul 2026), so it is 1.73x DEARER than baseline on haiku/vision/triage and a 37% capability DROP on sonnet (29.95 vs 47.21). It is EU insurance, correctly priced as insurance -- it should never be judged as a value lane.

openai.why: David's selection, 14 Aug 2026. Cheapest AND highest-scoring on the tiers that carry the volume (AA 51.24 vs Haiku 29.58, 77-79% cheaper). Golden set 8/8 on production prompts, 1 Aug 2026.

anthropic.why: First failover on a T1/T2 dropout. Months live, prompts tuned, production gate. Dearer than base by design -- continuity is worth a cost spike, and the spike must be visible.

scaleway.why: Ban and jurisdiction cover only (T3 / EU hosting). ONE-MODEL STANDBY. Never selected for value; reached only when both lanes above are unavailable. COST-EXEMPT by role: at 7.6-8.1x base on haiku/vision/triage it sits beyond the continuity tolerance, and that is correct -- a last resort is reached when the alternative is being DOWN or BANNED, where price is not the question. The tolerance therefore does not gate it; instead reaching it MUST raise an alert and be time-boxed, because an unnoticed week on the safety net is an 8x cost event nobody approved.

gemini.why: RUL-031/032: both general-LLM lanes failed at box coordinates (anthropic pre-14 Aug, openai since); Gemini is grounding-trained (native boxes + segmentation masks) at ~0.13x base cost. Canary design: it scans and refines, the active lane verifies every redaction -- a weak scanner degrades to more verify rounds, never to a leak.

decision.ruling: 1. OpenAI becomes the BASE usage model. Anthropic becomes the AUTO-FAILOVER. Scaleway remains the SAFETY NET for bans and downtime. 2. GUIDANCE: Anthropic is the main DESIGN tool and the guidance layer (development, review, architecture -- this session); OpenAI is the base USAGE model (in-app runtime on trustsquare.co). The two are separate concerns and must not be conflated: the tool that helps build the app is not the tool that must run inside it at volume.
decision.basis: Value on the register: gpt-5.6-luna AA 51.24 at $0.20/$1.20 vs claude-haiku-4-5 AA 29.58 at $1.00/$5.00 -- cheaper AND higher-scoring, 7.6x the value per dollar. Luna also outscores claude-sonnet-4-6 (47.21) at a thirteenth of its price.
